title: Protect Temperament While You Learn
coreMove: Preserve a gap between emotional pressure and committed action so the better tool remains reachable.
sourcePressure: The source says fear, reward, status, reciprocity, fairness, self-interest, memory, and self-serving distortions can break execution. People can know better and still act poorly when social or emotional pressure takes over. Wisdom is framed as reducing preventable mistakes, not eliminating all error.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The weak version is calm-down advice. The chapter must show knowledge becoming unavailable under pressure and the small behavioral gap that lets judgment return before action hardens.

sourceAnchors.name: Charlie Munger commencement speech
sourceAnchors.detail: The frozen source notes list a Charlie Munger commencement speech in the appendix alongside Munger and Buffett wisdom excerpts and checklist-like reminders; use only as a light book-level reference, not as a quoted source.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The Munger appendix points the same direction: wisdom is less about sounding brilliant than becoming harder to rush into ordinary preventable mistakes.

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person You direct address, retrospective It took her three weeks to see, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

exampleSpecs.domain: emergency department handoff after a senior physician snaps at a resident
exampleSpecs.audience: Rachel, a resident who knows the protocol but feels publicly humiliated
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether status threat makes her skip a clarifying question during a risky transfer
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Rachel writes the clarifying question on her glove cuff and asks it before signing the handoff, despite the heat in her face
exampleSpecs.firstImage: the alcohol-wipe smell sharp under fluorescent triage lights

exampleSpecs.domain: family estate meeting where one sibling frames revision as betrayal
exampleSpecs.audience: Mikkel, an executor trying not to let pride answer first
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether embarrassment over an old promise blocks a fair update after new tax numbers arrive
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Mikkel reads the new tax letter aloud, folds his first defensive note in half, and asks for ten minutes to recalculate before replying
exampleSpecs.firstImage: "You promised Dad," across a table with a tax letter between them

exampleSpecs.domain: commodity trading desk after a loss breaches the prewritten limit
exampleSpecs.audience: Catarina, a junior trader hearing the room call the dip temporary
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether fear of looking weak makes her ignore the loss limit she wrote while calm
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Catarina touches the printed loss-limit card taped under her monitor and exits the position before explaining herself to the desk lead
exampleSpecs.firstImage: At 9:36 a.m., Catarina watches copper drop through the red line on screen

exampleSpecs.domain: immigration interview prep when a client panics and wants to embellish
exampleSpecs.audience: Layla, a legal clinic volunteer who knows panic can make truth look insufficient
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether fear turns a fixable omission into a credibility problem
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Layla places the original document gap and the honest explanation on the same folder, then has the client practice the plain answer twice before adding anything
exampleSpecs.firstImage: You watch a client twist a folder corner until the paper fibers split

exampleSpecs.domain: startup outage response where the founder wants to blame a vendor publicly
exampleSpecs.audience: Andrew, an engineering lead with the incident timeline open
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether status defense corrupts the postmortem before the root cause is known
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Andrew locks the draft public post, adds a twelve-hour no-blame review line, and writes the unknowns under the knowns before Slack outrage becomes the official story
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a status page stuck on amber while Slack messages stack faster than alerts

exampleSpecs.domain: orchestra audition feedback after a conductor dismisses a musician too sharply
exampleSpecs.audience: Janek, an assistant conductor asked to deliver feedback without protecting his own authority
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether pride turns a correct technical note into a humiliating exchange that teaches nothing
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Janek crosses out the clever first sentence, names the single bowing issue, and invites one replay instead of defending the conductor's tone
exampleSpecs.firstImage: three crossed-out sentences on the back of an audition score

skillTargets: spot status threat hijacking a known rule
use prewritten limits when emotion rises
identify self-serving revision after the fact

tryThisNowSpec: Write one sentence you will use when pride or fear starts talking first: I need ten minutes before I turn this reaction into a decision.

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'
